edges.residual: The shared corpus fixes only gate-relevant finite fields and a Boolean standing-authorized witness; it does not encode the full StandingAuthority object or free-text metadata.
JSON field names and enum strings are lowered into Lean constructors; action identity and descriptive metadata are intentionally absent.
Assessment reasons, score, authority basis, and report flag are projected away; only the gate is compared.
The NumPy path evaluates the registered finite carrier, map, distance, and predicates but does not carry a proof object or generalize beyond the finite witness.
Only the observed Lipschitz constant and predicate-preservation result are compared.
JSON labels are lowered into the existing Lean TwoPoint carrier, discrete distance, collapseToBad map, and predicates; the source hash and semantic tokens are checked mechanically.
The richer Lean proof object is observed only through the registered 0-Lipschitz and non-preservation facts.
JSON serialization order and formatting are discarded when the edge set is loaded; graph vertices, directed edges, distinguished node, and mutation operator are preserved.
The executable mutation emits family-closure membership plus mutation provenance, not a general theorem over all dependency graphs.
String-labeled vertices and edge lists are lowered into the finite DNode inductive type and Boolean edge functions; source hash and mutation tokens are checked mechanically.
The Lean theorem observes only that the target co-parent is absent before and present after; it does not claim Bayesian conditional independence or constitutional significance.

agreements.scope: The 16 registered finite controller vectors only; this is not universal Python/Lean functional equivalence.
The registered two-point counterexample only. NumPy supplies a finite numerical witness; Lean supplies the proof. Agreement does not promote NumPy to a proof engine.
The registered four-node edge-addition witness only. It establishes a family-closure topology change, not a probabilistic Markov-blanket theorem or a constitutional gate.
